Update: I have taken an almost year long hiatus from this game to clear my mind, and I've come back to it to play with close friends and no one else. What I've gathered from my time back in the game, with no disrespect, is that the developer constantly makes decisions that are, what I would call, regressive. There are, of course, good parts of updates, but his updates seem to be mainly focused on new gimmicky bricks and maybe a graphical update every now and then, and less on actual optimization and bugfixes. Quite simply this game is the closest to a perfect sandbox I have ever played primarily due to the depth and intricate complexity offered by the build system, and the enjoyable fun from the damage system. The build system can best be described as essentially a Computer Aided Design (CAD) software with not only just bricks but also many other varieties of pieces with scalable sizes that allow for some of the most detailed creations in any block-based sandbox game. For a number the absolute smallest a brick can be is 1 cubic centimeter. Along with making creations so incredibly detailed, the selection of math bricks, sensors, and switches allow for builds with immensely complex logic systems. The game's build system also includes many other features allowing for quite literally almost limitless building possibilities. Many other games will say, "limitless possibilities" when they limit your parts usage, or how big your creations can be, or the game just doesn't have enough feature variety or optimization for you to create anything your mind comprehends. I mean it quite literally when I say Brick Rigs has limitless possibilities. In reality the only limitation is the build space, which is so massive it's almost always never a problem, and your computer's processing power, the primary limitation of what you can build, but this game is quite optimized for massive builds or part intense builds.

Besides the building systems, Brick Rigs has plenty of other features to allow for enjoyment outside of building. Brick Rigs has fairly stable multiplayer, being reliable most of the time, however on some occasions especially in public servers, desync and low frame rates can happen, mostly due to many players connecting at once and many vehicles being spawned in the same lobby. Otherwise, if you are just casually goofing around with your friends the multiplayer is fantastic. The game also has good map and gamemode variety, but could be greatly improved, along with weaponry for both your character and vehicles. Already the logic and math circuits that can be created allowed for incredibly advanced targeting, movement, and weapon systems, but there are much simpler to use weapon bricks allowing easy creation of tanks and planes. Along with these vehicle weapons, the character has fairly basic weapon options, but those weapons allow for quite enjoyable FPS gunplay.

One final thing to mention is factors outside of just the game, as Brick Rigs has a decently thriving Discord server, well populated with people consistently active, and new creations are always uploaded onto the workshop, and the game has some support for modding. Modding the game is not as easy as games like Garry's Mod or Left 4 Dead 2, but the mods for Brick Rigs open up a massive catalog of extra community made content that drastically improves almost every part of Brick Rigs, like more weapons, more bricks, more maps, and many mods that improve the game's quality of life.

Overall Brick Rigs has consistently remained my absolute favorite game since I started playing PC games in 2020 and I have never grown bored from the building and immense depth of the game's features, and that has only been expedited by the multiplayer allowing me to play with friends.
The only thing I think this game would need is a proper tutorial on how the build system works.

I've been a massive fan of this game for years and I hoped the 1.0 update would remove the things that really bugged me. Those were:
-The game is called Brick RIGS implying you're supposed to make vehicles, yet WHEELS don't work! If you drive faster than 50 kmh, you're playing Russian roulette as they randomly bounce and throw you off the cliff...

-Gears don't work. Instead of lower gears having more torque and less speed and higher ones having less torque and more speed, here, the higher the gear, the higher the power and speed! It's like a cross between LEGO digital designer and an open world LEGO game, is the simplest I can put it. Everyone has either played a LEGO game or had a go at Digital Designer, but here you get to play with what you've built. It's a fun thing to mess around with and see how far you can push the limit of both your own designs and creativity and how far you can push the physics engine! It's got an active community and the workshop is filled with great designs and builders (plug for my own workshop here). You can either play online or single player, but the latter is more for building a designing something as you can't get that much fun out of going things by yourself.

However, despite the good, there is some bad and I mean quite a lot of bad actually. The multiplayer is unstable when here's more than 1,000 bricks out, even after it was updated once. This has been improved with a full release, but multiplayer is still a bit buggy. Many servers are filled with kids mad with admin powers and I suggest generally avoiding joining random servers and instead making one with friends instead. There are some minor bugs and glitches, but none that I've found 'break the game'. While I did praise the community, many of them are screaming kids who don't know how to construct a proper sentence or argument from what I've seen (again, I tend to stay away from the discussions page to avoid being dragged into one). However, the biggest problem many have is the lack of constant updates. The games is built by one man and one man only who is working hard to make this game as good as he can with his limited free time, which I must applaud as there's no way I could ever make a game like this.

Overall, do I say this is worth it after all that criticism? Yes, I do. It's a fun game to design and create in and I've spent many hours as you can tell making tanks, planes, cars, buildings and set pieces. It's a very versatile game which you can spend hours in making anything from a humble hatchback to a massive aircraft carrier. It embodies the LEGO freedom we all wanted as a kid but couldn't get because we didn't have the right bricks. Let your imagination run free and stay away from this discussion page!
